title: Cuban piano style and great pianists
summary: He describes piano as bass and harmony and praises Benito.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Right. I want to come back to the basic roles of the instruments also. Let's take the piano, okay? I've noticed the Cuban piano style is very distinctive.

Now, I'm glad you brought that up. When these people started fooling around here, and they're trying to deviate the people mentality and calling our music the piano players, they (unintelligible). And every piano player here, or every orchestra here, when you hear a piano play behind the band, or you hear the same thing that was playing (singing), --

That other thing that I used to create in my orchestra, the piano played the left hand like a bass, the right hand to harmonize. And create -- I created with the piano and the bass three-part rhythm, beside the bongo, we created four.
Who were the great Cuban pianists?

Well, there was many (unintelligible). Perrochin was one, the outstanding piano player for years. Leelee and the (unintelligible). Now, when you talk of the Churanga, (unintelligible) was the classic. A fellow by the

name of (unintelligible) in Brazil was the more outstanding, to me, piano player that I have heard today. And I hate to say this. When the people talk about Perrochin, they talk about Leelee, it's because they never heard Benito, because if you have ever heard Benito, (unintelligible), you're going to find out how hard these people tried to copy. They never got into what Benito used to do.

And I was lucky enough to play with that man. And one later book that they released, for the first time I seen the picture of Benito. He died in Brazil -- went to Brazil at the end of the '30s. He died there. To me, he was one of the greatest true piano players that ever put his hands on a piano. And I thought (unintelligible) was the classic.
